items.title: Scène de crime horrible en Haïti: Une jeune femme hachée et décapitée avec la complicité de sa meilleure amie, la scène filmée
items.description: C'est l'une des vidéos les plus violentes et les plus cruelles que le monde ait jamais connues. D'une sauvagerie indescriptible, cette séquence montrant l'exécution à la machette d'une jeune internaute surnommée « Baby Love » secoue profondément Haïti. À l'origine de ce drame figure une enquête d'amateur sur l'application Snapchat, ayant mis en lumière les liaisons secrètes de l'influenceuse Esther Thomas, alias « Nice B », avec le chef du redoutable gang des 400 Mawozo. Fureur, vengeance et violation de la loi de l'omertà ont conduit au kidnapping puis à l'assassinat de la victime. Face à l'immense vague d'indignation provoquée par la diffusion en ligne de cette mise à mort, le Parquet de la Croix-des-Bouquets et la DCPJ ont lancé, le 5 septembre 2026, un avis de recherche contre l'influenceuse pour assassinat et association de malfaiteurs, illustrant de manière effroyable le climat de terreur qui gangrène le pays depuis 2021. Dans la pénombre d'une scène éclairée par des projecteurs et des lampes de téléphones portables, la sauvagerie a franchi un cap qui dépasse l'entendement. La victime, une jeune internaute connue sous le pseudonyme de « Baby Love », a été soumise à une agression d'une extrême brutalité. Dans une séquence vidéo de quelques minutes largement relayée sur Internet, la jeune femme, étendue au sol, est hachée et découpée vivante à la machette tour à tour par deux hommes et par sa propre amie, la tiktokeuse Esther Thomas, dite « Nice B ». Loin de chercher à se dissimuler, les agresseurs ont délibérément enregistré leur forfait afin de diffuser la vidéo à grande échelle sur les réseaux sociaux. Aux origines du drame : Enquête sur Snapchat, omertà et rage de vengeance https://netafrique.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/NetAfrique_Babylove_reportage_45s_paysage.mp4 Les motifs de cet acte d'une cruauté inimaginable trouvent leur racine dans l'univers virtuel. Tout a débuté lorsqu'une jeune internaute particulièrement observatrice a analysé des publications éphémères sur l'application Snapchat. En observant la couleur d'une chambre et la disposition d'un lit concordant entre deux comptes distincts, elle a publié une vidéo affirmant par « A + B » que son amie « Nice B » partageait en secret la vie du chef des 400 Mawozo, l'un des gangs les plus redoutés du pays. La publication insinuait également une complicité active de l'influenceuse au sein du réseau criminel. Saisie d'une rage noire face à ces révélations menaçant sa sécurité, l'influenceuse aurait réclamé « la tête » de l'internaute pour assouvir sa vengeance. La victime a ensuite été traquée, kidnappée puis livrée à ses bourreaux. Traquée par la justice : Le mandat d'arrêt contre Esther Thomas https://netafrique.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/fget.io_1788989457632.mp4 Face à l'immense vague d'indignation et à la diffusion de ces images insoutenables, l'appareil judiciaire haïtien est sorti de son silence. Par une réquisition datée du 5 septembre 2026, le Parquet près le Tribunal de première instance de la Croix-des-Bouquets a ordonné la recherche et l’arrestation immédiate d'Esther Thomas. Dans la foulée, la Police Nationale d'Haïti (PNH) et la Direction Centrale de la Police Judiciaire (DCPJ) ont diffusé un avis de recherche national ciblant « Nice B » ainsi que Darlens Duclona, alias « Enspektè tèt kale ». Tous deux sont formellement poursuivis pour des chefs d'accusation d'assassinat, de tentative d'assassinat et d'association de malfaiteurs, scellant la fin de la carrière de créatrice de contenu d'Esther Thomas et le début de sa cavale criminelle. Haïti sous le règne de la terreur : L’emprise des gangs et la propagande par l'image Ce crime odieux met en lumière la crise sécuritaire et humanitaire sans précédent qui ravage Haïti. Depuis l'assassinat du président Jovenel Moïse, survenu le 7 juillet 2021 dans sa résidence lors d'une attaque par un commando armé, l'effondrement des institutions étatiques a accéléré l’emprise des cartels de la mafia et des gangs armés comme les 400 Mawozo, fortement implantés à la Croix-des-Bouquets. Ces groupes criminels ont transformé la violence extrême en outil de propagande, d'intimidation et de domination psychologique en utilisant les réseaux sociaux pour amplifier l'impact de leurs actes. Les chiffres publiés par l'ONU pour les premiers mois de l'année 2026 témoignent de cette tragédie nationale : entre janvier et début juin 2026, au moins 2 310 personnes ont été tuées, 1 106 blessées et 99 enlevées dans le pays, abandonné à la loi de la jungle. L’article Scène de crime horrible en Haïti: Une jeune femme hachée et décapitée avec la complicité de sa meilleure amie, la scène filmée est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Yobe LG poll: ADC alleges exclusion by YSIEC
items.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu DAMATURU — The Yobe State chapter of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused the Yobe State Independent Electoral Commission, YSIEC, of excluding the party from crucial electoral information ahead of the 2026 local government election. The party threatened to seek legal redress and organise peaceful protests if the commission fails to address its concerns. ADC made the allegations in a letter of concern addressed to the Chairman of YSIEC, expressing what it described as “serious concern and disappointment” over the commission’s alleged failure to communicate election guidelines, timetable and other electoral decisions affecting its participation. The party said equal and meaningful access to electoral information was essential to the lawful participation of political parties in an election. It therefore demanded evidence of when, how and through which official channel the relevant guidelines, timetable and electoral decisions were communicated to it. “We therefore request clear evidence of when, how and through what official channel the relevant Guidelines, timetable and electoral decisions were communicated to ADC,” the party stated. According to ADC, failure to properly notify it of electoral requirements could prejudice its ability to participate fully in the council election. The party cited Sections 7, 40 and 197 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Third Schedule, applicable electoral laws and YSIEC regulations in support of its concerns. ADC warned that it would pursue all lawful avenues if any action or omission by the commission affected its participation in the electoral process. “ADC hereby puts YSIEC on notice that, if our lawful rights or participation have been prejudiced by any failure of notification, we will pursue every lawful avenue available to protect our rights,” it stated. The party said such measures could include legal action, media engagement, social media advocacy and peaceful public protest. ADC also called on the commission to provide clarification and take appropriate corrective action if its participation had been affected by any failure of notification. The letter, dated September 2026, was addressed to the YSIEC Chairman, with copies sent to the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, the Yobe State Government, the Political Adviser to the Governor, the Commissioner of Police, the state command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and the Department of State Services. As of the time of filing this report, YSIEC had not publicly responded to the allegations contained in the ADC letter. The development comes as political parties prepare for the 2026 local government election in the state. The post Yobe LG poll: ADC alleges exclusion by YSIEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Inauguration du complexe industriel TEXFORCES-BF : désormais des tenues militaires « made in Burkina »
items.description: Le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a procédé, le mercredi 9 septembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, à l’inauguration du complexe industriel de Textile des forces du Burkina Faso (TEXFORCES-BF). D’un coût d’investissement de 17 milliards de francs CFA, cette infrastructure industrielle entend renforcer la transformation locale du coton, répondre aux besoins d’habillement des Forces de défense et de sécurité et contribuer à la création d’emplois. Lancé en avril 2024, le complexe industriel de Textile des forces du Burkina Faso (TEXFORCES-BF) est prêt à produire ses premières tenues militaires. L’inauguration a été faite par le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le mercredi 9 septembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso. Avec un coût d’investissement de 17 milliards de francs CFA, ce complexe industriel stratégique est implanté sur un site de 30 hectares à Logofourousso, dans l’arrondissement 7 de la capitale économique du Burkina Faso. Selon le chef de l’Etat, cette infrastructure est un symbole de souveraineté. « La souveraineté ne se décrète pas, elle se construit par l’action, elle se produit, elle se défend », a-t-il laissé entendre. A en croire le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, ce joyau est né de la volonté souveraine du peuple du Burkina Faso de transformer lui-même ses ressources, d’habiller ses vaillantes forces combattantes ainsi que la population civile. « Ce complexe est unique en son genre dans la sous-région. C’est un message fort parce que ce ne sont pas des investisseurs étrangers qui sont venus le faire. Ce ne sont pas des capitaux étrangers. C’est propre à nous. C’est un complexe qui a été financé par le peuple burkinabè pour faire tout ce que le peuple veut en matière de textile », a souligné le président du Faso. Il a invité le peuple burkinabè à croire en ses capacités. Avec ses unités de filature, de tissage-tricotage, de finition et de confection, TEXFORCES-BF ambitionne de constituer un maillon important de la chaîne nationale du coton et du textile. Le complexe doit notamment produire des tenues destinées aux Forces de défense et de sécurité, mais également des effets d’habillement pour les populations civiles. Réduire la dépendance vis-à-vis des importations A travers cette coupure de ruban, le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a officiellement lancé les activités de TEXFORCES-BF. Selon le président du conseil d’administration de TEXFORCES-BF, le général de brigade Ismaël Kiswendsida Souampa Diaouari, le complexe dispose de capacités pouvant atteindre annuellement 20 millions de mètres de tissu au tissage, 20 millions de mètres en finition-teinture et entre 4 et 6 millions de tenues confectionnées. Le complexe prévoit également une production pouvant atteindre un million de paires de chaussettes par an. Une unité de tricotage à plat est, par ailleurs, destinée à la production de cols, poignets et articles connexes. A entendre le président du conseil d’admi-nistration, environ 1 300 ouvriers ont participé à la construction des infrastructures et à l’installation des équipe-ments. Plusieurs centaines de jeunes Burkinabè ont, par ailleurs, été formés aux métiers industriels. « Avec la montée en puissance de l’entreprise, l’objectif affiché est d’atteindre environ 20 000 emplois directs et de soutenir potentiellement plus de 60 000 emplois et moyens d’existence dans l’écosystème coton-textile, logistique, commercial et des services », a indiqué le général de brigade Diaouari. Selon le ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, qui a livré le discours du président du Faso, la mise en place de cette infrastructure vise à réduire progressivement la dépendance du Burkina Faso vis-à-vis des importations et à accroître la transformation locale des matières premières. « Nous ne pouvons pas continuer à produire la matière première, exporter les emplois qu’elle peut créer et importer ensuite les produits issus de notre propre richesse », a-t-il souligné. Pour lui, cette orientation s’inscrit dans une démarche de consolidation de la souveraineté écono-mique, technologique et industrielle du Burkina Faso. Le ministre a aussi insisté sur le rôle des producteurs de coton dans cette chaîne de valeur. « Cette usine est aussi la vôtre », leur a-t-il lancé. Il s’agit, selon lui, de rapprocher le monde rural du monde industriel et de faire en sorte que la transformation du coton profite davantage aux différents acteurs de la filière. A l’écouter, la chaîne de transformation doit également intégrer les stylistes, designers, modélistes, couturiers, commerçants, logisticiens et autres acteurs de l’écosystème textile. L’objectif affiché est de favoriser l’émergence d’un « made in Burkina Faso » reposant sur la production locale, la qualité et la créativité. Noufou NEBIE

items.title: Apple’s new boss starts with big gamble on costly first folding iPhone
items.description: John Ternus has entered his second week as Apple’s chief executive, and the company has revealed the first major change to the iPhone since its release almost 20 years ago. Ternus, who took on Apple’s top job after Tim Cook stepped down , was onstage Wednesday at the company’s annual product release event, in front of large images of the first foldable iPhone. With a book-style format, the new iPhone, dubbed the Duo, is the largest-ever model. And with a US starting price of $1,999 (£1,475) going up to $3,200, it is also the most expensive. UK prices start at £1,999. Ternus said the Duo was “inspired by the iPad” but called the folding features “fluid and completely intuitive.” The foldable phone has been a work in progress at Apple for several years. When unfolded, the new Duo looks like a small iPad. When folded in half, it looks like a wider iPhone. Ternus said during the event that Apple wanted to avoid the look and feel of other foldable smart phones on the market, which he said “feel like two phones stuck together… making a larger screen feel much smaller.” The Duo, he said, is the “result of a series of remarkable innovations that we think will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone.” Ternus was directly involved in developing the foldable iPhone as he spent many years as a top executive inside Apple’s hardware division before being tapped earlier this year as Cook’s successor. The new foldable iPhone can operate in two forms. Ben Wood, chief analyst at technology research firm FDM CCS Insight, said it was likely Ternus’s promotion was timed specifically “to coincide with what will be arguably one of the biggest iPhone launches for many years”. “Nothing happens by accident at Apple,” Wood added. Carolina Milanesi, an analyst at Creative Strategies who attended the Wednesday presentation, said the spotlight on Ternus made it feel “almost like he was a product himself.” Altering the design of the iPhone may address some criticism that Apple has yet to land a major product hit or truly exciting innovation since the first iPhone came out in 2007. “The foldable risks becoming a premium-priced ornament in the portfolio, imparting badge value but not meaningful growth,” said Dipanjan Chatterjee, an analyst at Forrester. Previously, the highest starting price of the newest iPhone was $900 (£664). Apple also revealed on Wednesday the new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, which in the US start at $1,199 (£855) and $1,299 (£959) respectively. Chatterjee said the foldable iPhone could go the way of Apple’s Vision Pro headset, which the company priced at $3,699 (£2,729) and has not been a hit with buyers. Or, he said, it could be the company’s next Apple Watch which, while not as popular as the iPhone, is bought by millions of people each year. The way people have become accustomed to the way the iPhone operates is another potential hurdle to Apple seeing big sales of the new design. “Foldables are interesting devices”, Milanesi noted. “A lot of people are intrigued by it, but the software and the learning curve that you have from moving from a traditional phone to a foldable is real.” Wood noted that the current market for foldable smartphones from the likes of Samsung and Huawei make up only 2% of smartphone sales. Even with Apple’s version likely driving interest and demand, sales are only expected to reach 4% of the total market in the next decade, according to data and analytics firm FDM CCM Insight. The iPhone has been Apple’s top-selling product and accounts for more than half of the company’s sales each year. In recent quarters, the company has boasted that the iPhone is more in demand than ever , with the latest version of the device becoming its most successful product launch . The company also revealed more about the coming relaunch of its audio and chat assistant Siri, which it now calls Siri AI. Starting with the iPhone 18, the bot will now be able to access information on a person’s phone, such as messages and emails, to find information, answer queries, and take action on a person’s behalf. Some Siri AI features will also be available on the new Apple Watch, including the ability to take notes on conversations and transcribe them, if the wearer enables the feature. Ternus referred to new AI-enabled capabilities on the iPhone as an “intelligent personal hub” and admitted that Apple would be using “the most private details of your daily life.” He insisted that all of it will remain private, with the AI features often running “on device”, meaning not through third-party companies. And when a third party is required for a function, Ternus said it will remain private on a remote server or in the cloud. “Others see that data as something to collect and store”, Ternus said. “Here, not even Apple can access what’s yours.”

items.title: Bensaid : les alliés du « PAM » au gouvernement ont rejeté nos propositions sur le pouvoir d’achat
items.description: Le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) affirme avoir soumis à ses partenaires de la majorité gouvernementale plusieurs propositions destinées à préserver le pouvoir d’achat durant les années de sécheresse. Selon Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid, ces propositions auraient été rejetées par les autres composantes de la majorité, alors que le parti remet aujourd’hui cette question au cœur de son programme électoral. Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid, membre de la direction collégiale du PAM, affirme que sa formation avait présenté à ses partenaires de la majorité gouvernementale, durant les années de sécheresse ayant marqué l’actuelle législature, les mesures figurant aujourd’hui dans son programme électoral en matière de protection du pouvoir d’achat. Selon lui, ces propositions avaient été rejetées dans leur ensemble, empêchant ainsi leur mise en œuvre. Lors d’une rencontre organisée ce mercredi soir à Marrakech, le responsable du PAM a ainsi remis sur la table la nécessité de réorienter l’action gouvernementale. Il a notamment plaidé pour une approche davantage fondée sur « le travail et la proximité », par opposition à ce qu’il considère comme une réponse insuffisamment adaptée aux réalités quotidiennes des Marocains. « Pendant quatre ans, on nous a dit que les tomates (dans le Souss) étaient à 3 dirhams. Mais quelqu’un qui vit à Marrakech, Rabat ou Casablanca va-t-il se rendre dans le Souss pour acheter ce produit de première nécessité ? », a-t-il lancé, mettant en avant la question de l’accessibilité réelle des produits de base pour les ménages. Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid a par ailleurs rappelé qu’il s’agissait de la première expérience du PAM au sein d’un gouvernement, tout en revendiquant les résultats obtenus par ses ministres dans plusieurs secteurs. Une manière également de se démarquer de son principal allié au sein de l’Exécutif, le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI), qui a participé à plusieurs gouvernements depuis sa création au milieu des années 1970. « C’est la première fois que nous assumons la responsabilité », a-t-il déclaré, avant de placer les prochaines échéances électorales au centre du défi pour sa formation. Le responsable du PAM est également sur les polémiques ayant marqué l’actuelle législature autour de soupçons de conflits d’intérêts, d’enrichissement illicite ou encore de pratiques liées à l’économie de rente. Sans désigner explicitement de responsables, il a accusé « certains » acteurs de tenter, durant la campagne, « d’acheter les consciences des Marocains ». « Nous voulons nous adresser au peuple marocain, et non aux entreprises. Nous voulons nous adresser à la jeunesse marocaine, et non aux personnes », a-t-il affirmé. Pour Bensaid, la campagne électorale ne doit toutefois pas se résumer à la conquête d’un siège. Elle doit également permettre d’établir un dialogue direct avec les électeurs autour des propositions avancées par les partis. « Aujourd’hui, il ne suffit pas seulement de gagner un siège ou de faire élire notre candidat. Il faut aussi dialoguer avec les Marocains et les convaincre de notre programme électoral », a-t-il soutenu. Le ministre chargé de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication a également mis en avant le « Pacte pour l’intégration des jeunes » inscrit dans le programme électoral du PAM. Selon lui, les jeunes Marocains ne réclament pas de privilèges particuliers, mais souhaitent avant tout bénéficier d’une formation de haut niveau, accéder à des emplois dignes et décents et être traités sur un pied d’égalité dans l’ensemble des provinces et des régions. Le responsable politique a enfin défendu le choix de son parti de présenter des engagements chiffrés dans son programme électoral. Cette précision, estime-t-il, aurait placé certains acteurs face à leurs responsabilités et alimenté, en retour, les débats et les échanges de critiques. « Nous avons réussi dans certains secteurs et échoué sur certains points. Il n’y a pas de problème à le reconnaître », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que la reconnaissance des difficultés constitue précisément le préalable à la recherche de nouvelles solutions. Selon Bensaid, une période de crise peut parfaitement survenir au cours d’une législature. Ce qui pose problème, à ses yeux, est de refuser de la reconnaître et de donner l’impression que « tout va bien » malgré les difficultés rencontrées. The post Bensaid : les alliés du « PAM » au gouvernement ont rejeté nos propositions sur le pouvoir d’achat appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tinubu’s wife empowers 500 women in Ebonyi
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has distributed empowerment items to 500 indigent women in Ebonyi State to support them in starting new businesses or improving existing enterprises. The items included deep freezers, gas cookers with ovens, power generators and industrial grinding machines. Tinubu, who was represented by the wife of the Ebonyi State Governor, Mrs Mary-Maudline Uzoamaka Nwifuru, said the empowerment programme was being implemented simultaneously in the five states of the South-East. She said the initiative was made possible through the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs. According to her, the programme was designed to empower 18,000 women nationwide, with 500 beneficiaries selected from each state and the Federal Capital Territory. She said: “This presentation is taking place across the five states of the zone simultaneously. “This programme has been made possible through the Office of the SSA to the President on Sustainable Development Goals. “The initiative was first launched in Abuja for the North-Central zone in February 2025, followed by the distribution of empowerment items in the South-South zone on April 25, 2026, and the South-West zone on August 23, 2025. “By the end of the nationwide rollout of this initiative, 18,000 women would have been empowered across the country, with 500 beneficiaries selected from each state and the FCT.” She said the programme aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Initiative, particularly in recognising the critical role women play in nation-building. She urged the beneficiaries to use the items judiciously to achieve the objectives of the programme. The representative of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on SDGs, Dr Ify Ukaegbu, also urged the beneficiaries not to sell the items. Ukaegbu said the intervention was aimed at expanding economic opportunities for indigent and vulnerable women across the country. Some of the beneficiaries expressed appreciation to the President’s wife and the wife of the Ebonyi State Governor for the gesture, saying the items would enable them to become self-reliant and support their families. They pledged to use the items judiciously, adding that the intervention came at a time when they needed support to establish sustainable means of livelihood. The post Tinubu’s wife empowers 500 women in Ebonyi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 24-Hour Economy was born from Ghana’s 48-year development plan – Nii Moi Thompson
items.description: Chairman of the National Development Planning Committee (NDPC), Dr Nii Moi Thompson, has revealed that government’s flagship 24-Hour Economy Programme was drawn from Ghana’s 48-year Development Plan. According to him, the 24-hour economy is one of the few key initiatives that emerged from the long-term development framework, although the plan itself was not legislated. “Actually, the 24-hour economy came from the 48 Development Plan. It’s one of the few things that have actually come out of it,” he said on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday. Dr Thompson explained that the NDC adopted the 24-hour economy from the development plan despite the failure to legislate the broader framework. “But the 48 Development Plan, as in its entirety, should have been legislated, but it wasn’t. But the government, the NDC, removed that from the 48 Development Plan. So the 24-hour economy actually came from the 48 development plan,” he said. He said other initiatives, including the naming of the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, also originated from the plan. “The name of the Ministry of Sports and Recreation came from the 48 development plan,” he said. Dr Thompson said the Ghana Agency for Development Cooperation was another initiative linked to the plan and was currently being developed between the National Development Planning Committee and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. “We have something known as the Ghana Agency for Development Cooperation, which is currently being developed between NDPs and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to help form soft power for Ghana and Global Affairs,” he said. Assessing the implementation of the 24-hour economy, Dr Thompson said those behind the programme had made progress, particularly in securing investments across different business categories. “From the perspective of those who came up with the idea, I think they’ve done pretty well. You have to understand that they are operating across a spectrum of businesses, from small to large,” he said. He noted that large businesses often require time before investments begin to deliver results. “Usually, it takes the gestation period for big businesses take a while to get, and I think they put a lot of effort into it. They’ve lined up a lot of investments. It will take a while for those to catch on,” he said. However, Dr Thompson said the programme must increasingly focus on small and medium-sized enterprises over the next two years. “My expectation is that in the next two years, they will focus more on the SMEs also, so that you cover the whole spectrum,” he said. He said job creation must also remain central to the programme, particularly because existing businesses account for a significant share of new jobs. “From our understanding, there are efforts on the way to handle that aspect of it,” he said. Dr Thompson added that the government must address not only unemployment but also underemployment and poor-quality jobs. “The issue of dealing with the quality of existing jobs is one of those legs that I expect them to work on in the next two years,” he said.

items.title: Unilorin don urges FG to prioritise aquaculture
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi ILORIN: A Professor of Agriculture and Fisheries at the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, Wasiu Adeyemi Jimoh, has urged the Federal Government to make sustainable aquaculture a strategic component of Nigeria’s food security, nutrition and economic development agenda. Jimoh said increased investment in aquaculture could accelerate the development of a resilient, environmentally sustainable and globally competitive industry capable of creating jobs, reducing dependence on fish imports and contributing significantly to national economic growth. He made the call while delivering the 306th inaugural lecture of the University of Ilorin, titled, “Green Feeds, Healthy Fish: Enhancing Aquaculture Productivity,” at the university auditorium on Monday. The don said the sector could be strengthened through increased investment in research, innovation, human capacity development and the commercialisation of locally developed technologies. According to him, “Investment in aquaculture will accelerate the transition towards a resilient, environmentally sustainable, and globally competitive industry, capable of creating employment, reducing import dependence, and contributing significantly to national economic development.” He added that strategic implementation of the proposed measures would transform aquaculture into a resilient, environmentally restorative and economically viable sector. Jimoh said the development of the sector was essential to achieving food and nutrition security, creating sustainable employment and improving livelihoods for present and future generations. He explained that his research had focused on developing alternatives to conventional fish feed ingredients through the use of plant-based protein sources, phytogenic additives and circular-economy principles. “These efforts aimed to reduce dependence on fishmeal and soybean meal, optimise nutrient utilisation, enhance fish health, and improve economic sustainability for fish farmers,” he said. The professor noted that fish remained one of the most nutrient-dense and accessible sources of protein, providing high-quality amino acids, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins and minerals. He said fish was particularly important in developing countries where malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies remained challenges, adding that it served as both a source of nutrition and livelihood for millions of people. Jimoh also called on feed manufacturers, veterinary professionals, fish health specialists and regulatory agencies to formulate, certify and promote functional aquafeeds for fish farmers. He advocated the routine use of aquafeeds containing probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and natural immunostimulants, saying they could strengthen disease prevention, reduce antibiotic misuse and improve fish welfare and productivity. “Fish occupy a unique and irreplaceable position in the global landscape, influencing dietary patterns, shaping economic activities, and fostering traditions that are deeply rooted in historical and ecological contexts. “Fish are not merely food sources but a lifeline that sustains billions of people worldwide. From the bustling fish markets of Asia to the artisanal fisheries of Africa, fish form the bedrock of diets, livelihoods, and communities,” he said. items.title: Gombe JPDA DG highlights three years of projects
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Director-General of the Gombe State Joint Projects Development and Essential Social Services Agency, JPDA, Dr Mahmood Yusuf, has highlighted the agency’s projects across the state in his three years in office, describing the period as one of institutional growth, leadership experience and grassroots development. Yusuf, a Fellow of the Nigerian Institute of Building, FNIOB, also expressed appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the opportunity to serve in the position. The agency, formerly known as the Gombe State Joint Projects Development Agency, has expanded its mandate to include essential social services and developmental interventions across the state. Reflecting on his stewardship, Yusuf said his three years in office had provided valuable lessons in leadership, public service, accountability and human relations. “Working directly under His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has made me understand that leadership is ultimately about the impact one makes in the lives of others,” he said. He said the experience had broadened his understanding of public service, particularly the importance of prudence, effective communication and listening to diverse opinions. According to Yusuf, the agency has executed projects across the state’s 11 local government areas, covering infrastructure, grassroots administration, markets, traditional institutions, security facilities and renewable energy. In Akko Local Government Area, he listed the reconstruction of the local government secretariat and Gona Emir’s Palace, installation of solar streetlights in Kumo and Tumfure, and construction of the Akko West LCDA Secretariat in Pindiga and Akko North LCDA Secretariat in Amada. In Balanga, the agency provided a one-megawatt solar mini-grid for Tallasse and Swa communities and constructed the Balanga South LCDA Secretariat in Bambam. Billiri benefited from the reconstruction of the Gada-Uku-Sansani Bridge, construction of a police outpost at Amtawalam, reconstruction of Kantoma Market, construction of the Billiri Grains Market and the Billiri West LCDA Secretariat at Tal. In Dukku, projects included a motor park, grains and cattle market, solar streetlights and the Dukku North LCDA Secretariat at Malala. Yusuf said Funakaye received the reconstruction of the Emir’s Palace and 12 district head palaces, construction of 66 shops in Bajoga, solar streetlights in Bajoga and Ashaka, and the Funakaye South LCDA Secretariat in Tongo. In Gombe Local Government Area, the agency reconstructed the Idi Shopping Complex and Gombe Emir’s Palace, as well as constructed the Gombe South LCDA Secretariat in Bolari. Projects in Kwami included the reconstruction and furnishing of 11 district head palaces, solar streetlights in several communities and the Kwami West LCDA Secretariat in Bojude. In Kaltungo, the agency reconstructed the local government secretariat, constructed market stalls and built the Kaltungo East LCDA Secretariat at Tula Wange. Nafada Local Government Area benefited from the construction of its local government secretariat, solar streetlights in Nafada and surrounding communities, and the Nafada South LCDA Secretariat at Birin Fulani. In Shongom, projects included part of the local government secretariat, seven district head palaces, a 650KWH solar mini-grid in Filiya and the Pero-Chonge LCDA Secretariat. In Yamaltu/Deba, the agency provided fencing, solar streetlights and a solar-powered borehole with four fetching points at the National Agricultural Land Development Authority, NALDA, Market in Kwadon. Solar streetlights were also installed in Deba, Dadin Kowa, Hinna, Kwadon, Wajari, Gwani, Shinga and Wade, while the Yamaltu East and Yamaltu West LCDA secretariats were constructed at Dadin Kowa and Zambuk respectively. Yusuf further disclosed that the construction of the Gombe State Council of Emirs and Chiefs Secretariat had reached about 95 per cent completion. He said the project, when completed, would provide a befitting institutional structure for traditional leadership in the state. The JPDA boss attributed the achievements to the support and guidance of Governor Inuwa Yahaya, as well as the cooperation of stakeholders, staff and communities. He expressed optimism that the agency would continue to contribute to the implementation of projects aimed at improving the living conditions of residents. “I sincerely thank everyone for their unwavering support throughout this journey. The achievements recorded are a product of collective effort, and I hope we will continue to work together to move our dear state forward,” Yusuf said. items.title: Gombe women mobilise over 6,000 for unity summit
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — More than 6,000 women from across Gombe State on Wednesday converged on the APC Square, Gombe, for the maiden Gombe Women’s Unity and Progress Summit convened by Dr Zainab Jamil Gwamna. The summit, held under the theme, “Stronger Voices, United Women, Greater Impact,” brought together women from the state’s 11 local government areas and 13 Local Council Development Areas, including entrepreneurs, professionals, community leaders, political stakeholders and women advocates. According to a statement by Ibrahim Sani Shawai, spokesperson to the APC governorship candidate in Gombe State, Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, the summit was designed to promote unity, empowerment, mentorship and greater participation of women in governance and socio-economic development. Speaking at the event, the convener, Dr Zainab Gwamna, said the initiative was aimed at building a united women’s movement capable of supporting one another and creating opportunities for younger generations. “This summit is about bringing Gombe women together to discover our collective strength and understand that the success of one woman should open doors for another,” she said. “We must mentor our young girls, support women in business and professions, strengthen our families and contribute meaningfully to our communities.” Gwamna commended the turnout, describing it as an indication of the potential of women to contribute to social and economic development. She also commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for programmes targeted at women and youths, while appreciating her husband, Dr Jamil Gwamna, for his support. The convener urged participants to take the lessons and relationships developed at the summit back to their communities, with emphasis on mentoring young girls, skills acquisition, confidence building and economic self-reliance. Also speaking, the wife of the Gombe State Governor, Dr Asma’u Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, commended the initiative and the turnout of women from across the state. She reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to programmes aimed at improving the welfare, empowerment and economic wellbeing of women and youths. “Women are indispensable partners in the development of our families, communities and the state,” she said. “I commend Dr Zainab Gwamna for bringing women together through this important summit and for creating a platform where they can learn, connect and support one another.” Dr Asma’u encouraged the participants to sustain the spirit of unity, cooperation and mutual support demonstrated at the gathering. Participants from different professional and community backgrounds also commended the initiative, saying sustained collaboration, mentorship and economic empowerment were important to increasing women’s participation in development. Some participants expressed optimism that the networks established at the summit would continue beyond the event and create opportunities for women and young girls across the state. The gathering also had political undertones, with some political stakeholders saying the mobilisation could strengthen the grassroots support base of the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the central message of the summit was the need for women to support one another, mentor younger generations and use collective action to promote social and economic development in Gombe State. items.title: Polaris Bank manager killed in Imo kidnapping attack
items.description: OWERRI — Polaris Bank has expressed grief over the killing of one of its branch managers, identified as Mr Ossy, who was reportedly shot dead by suspected kidnappers at the Federal University of Technology, Owerri, FUTO, Imo State. The incident occurred on Sunday, September 6, 2026, within the university premises, while the banker, who was based in Owerri, was reportedly taking his children to the institution. Two female students were also reportedly abducted during the incident. In a statement issued on Tuesday and signed by the Head, Brand Management and Corporate Communication of Polaris Bank, Rasheed Bolarinwa, the bank said the deceased was attacked by hoodlums while taking his children to the university. The bank said his children managed to escape, but he was killed in the incident. “We are deeply saddened by the tragic death of our Branch Manager and extend our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and loved ones during this difficult time. “The unfortunate incident occurred on Sunday, when he was accosted by the hoodlums, and while the children managed to escape from the scene, he was not that lucky,” the statement said. The bank said the incident was being investigated by relevant law enforcement agencies and expressed confidence that the circumstances surrounding the killing would be established. “Our thoughts and prayers remain with the family of the deceased, and we respectfully urge the public to allow the authorities to complete their investigations,” it added. Meanwhile, the management of FUTO confirmed that a visitor to the university was fatally shot during the incident and that two female students were reportedly abducted. In a statement signed by the Registrar, Chinonso Uba, the university said the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the circumstances were under investigation by security agencies. “Management is engaging with the appropriate authorities regarding the safe recovery of the students,” the statement said. The university assured students, staff, parents and other members of the community that their safety remained a priority, adding that additional security measures were being implemented in collaboration with security agencies. It urged members of the university community to remain calm and vigilant, avoid unnecessary movement and promptly report suspicious activities. Following the incident, FUTO management met with the Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, on Monday over security concerns around the university and its host communities. Bosso reportedly assured the university management of intensified security around the institution and neighbouring communities, particularly the Ihiagwa, Eziobodo, Obinze and Nekede axes. Meanwhile, a source who spoke on condition of anonymity said a proposed peaceful protest by some students over the killing was cancelled following the university’s reaffirmation of its ban on unruly and rowdy gatherings after examinations. The ban was adopted by the FUTO Senate at its 495th and 501st meetings held on August 31, 2023, and April 29, 2024, respectively, following concerns over the destruction of university property, particularly during celebrations by graduating students. The university management reaffirmed the prohibition at its seventh meeting held on Monday, September 7, 2026, warning students against activities capable of disrupting peace on the campus and in neighbouring communities. The prohibited activities include rowdy behaviour, public revelry, disorderly conduct, littering, indiscriminate disposal of waste, blocking or obstructing roads and entrances, and damaging or defacing university property. The management also warned against any conduct capable of threatening the safety and security of the university community. The post Polaris Bank manager killed in Imo kidnapping attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kintinian : trois blessés graves dans une collision impliquant trois motos
items.description: Un grave accident de la circulation s’est produit ce mercredi, aux environs de 17 heures, sur la route principale reliant Boukaria, dans la commune urbaine de Kintinian, à la ville de Siguiri. L’accident, qui a impliqué trois engins à deux roues, a fait trois blessés graves, dont une mère de famille se trouvant dans un état jugé très critique. Selon les premiers éléments recueillis sur les circonstances du drame, deux motocyclistes, dont un conducteur de moto-taxi, circulaient l’un derrière l’autre dans la même direction. C’est au moment où un troisième motard, qui s’apprêtait à traverser la route, aurait brusquement barré leur passage que l’accident s’est produit. En tentant d’éviter l’obstacle, les deux premières motos seraient entrées en collision. Dans le choc, le conducteur de moto-taxi, sa cliente et l’enfant de cette dernière ont été grièvement blessés. Alertée par les autorités locales, l’ambulance spéciale de la Société Aurifère de Guinée (SAG) s’est rendue d’urgence sur les lieux. Les victimes ont été rapidement évacuées vers des structures sanitaires pour y recevoir les soins nécessaires. Quant aux trois motos impliquées dans l’accident, elles ont été saisies et transportées au commissariat de police de Boukaria, en attendant que les responsabilités soient officiellement établies. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Kintinian : trois blessés graves dans une collision impliquant trois motos est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: What the NBA must do to help Nigeria, Africa grow — Ex-Liberian President Weah
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri Despite the controversy that trailed his selection as keynote speaker at the recent Annual General Conference of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), George Weah, immediate past President of the Republic of Liberia, took the legal body to task, outlining what it must do to help the country and the continent. Weah, who served as President of Liberia from 2018 to January 2024 before losing his bid for re-election to Joseph Boakai, insisted that the NBA, as the continent’s biggest umbrella body of lawyers with a membership of over 150,000, must shed mediocrity and stand firmly for justice in order to safeguard the rule of law and democracy in Africa. Speaking on the theme “Beyond Limits,” the former footballer who swapped the pitch for politics maintained that Nigeria holds the key to the promise of the entire continent. According to him, “When the NBA decides to go beyond limits, the legal architecture of Africa itself grows stronger.” Addressing legal eggheads at the conference held in Port Harcourt, the former Ballon d’Or winner said: “I want to thank you for choosing a theme as bold as ‘Beyond Limits.’ “When I first heard it, I smiled, because if my own life has taught me one thing, it is that limits are very often not the walls we think they are. They are only the edge of what someone has tried so far. “I did not come into this hall as a lawyer, and I will not pretend to be one. I grew up in the ghetto of ‘Gibraltar’ in Monrovia, Liberia, where very few people believed that a boy raised largely by his grandmother would one day stand on the world’s biggest football stages, or take an oath as President of the Republic of Liberia. “Allow me to speak to you about two things today: first, the Bar and the Bench as guardians of our democracy, and the dangers that threaten that guardianship in West Africa today; and second, what it means for our peoples and our continent to truly go beyond limits, not in slogan, but in substance. “Let me start with a simple truth I came to understand not as a student of law, but as a man who has sat in the highest office of a nation. “Democracy does not survive on the strength of elections alone. Elections are the doorway into democracy, not the house itself. “What holds the house up, what keeps the roof from collapsing on the people who live inside it, are institutions, and among the most important of these, in every serious nation, is an independent judiciary, protected by a fearless, principled Bar. “And let me be plain about something else, because it is often the more dangerous of the two threats to democracy. “The danger is not only that soldiers might seize power in the night, or that a defeated candidate might refuse to leave office. “It is also that a leader who arrives in office through a free and fair election can, over time and often gradually, begin to govern like the very dictators the ballot was meant to guard against, leaning on the judiciary until it bends to his will, and strong-arming the legislature until it becomes an echo chamber rather than a check on his power. “A tyrant with a certificate of return is still a tyrant. Democracy, properly understood, does not end on election night. It is tested every single day afterward, in how power treats the courts and the parliament that exist to restrain it.” Continuing, ex-President Weah argued that the rule of law is not an abstract phrase for law school lecture halls. He described it as the practical guarantee that a citizen’s rights depend not on who holds office or what favors they can secure, but on equal protection under the law for everyone, regardless of status or position in society. “The moment that guarantee weakens, everything else in a nation weakens with it: investment, security, public trust, and peace itself. “And here is the uncomfortable part: this danger does not only come from the coup-makers who seize power in the night. It also comes from governments that call themselves democratic, through budget manipulation, questionable appointments, pressure on judges, and a mindset that treats courts as a convenience rather than a check. “We have seen nations where a judiciary’s own budget must first pass through the executive it is meant to hold accountable. “We have seen special courts created not to deliver justice but to secure political outcomes, and dozens of judges dismissed in a single stroke by presidential decree. “And we have seen, across our region since 2020, an unsettling pattern of soldiers stepping over constitutions altogether. “I raise these examples because this Bar, to which you belong and have gathered here in your thousands, cannot afford to assume that Nigeria, or Liberia, or any of us, is somehow immune. “A court’s decision must mean what it says, without anyone’s political permission; it is what protects a nation from sliding, gradually but progressively, into the very conditions we condemn when soldiers do it with guns. “This is why I say to you: the Nigerian Bar Association is not merely a professional association negotiating welfare for its members. “You are a standing sentinel of this Republic’s democracy. When the Bar is silent, courts become easier to capture. “When the Bar speaks with one voice, as guardians of the bench, the executive branch thinks twice before even dreaming of interference. “That tradition is not decoration. It is duty, because protecting the independence of your courts, and the rights of the ordinary Nigerian citizen, is protecting democracy itself, here in Nigeria and across the region,” he added. Contending that Africa’s limits are not a matter of talent, Weah identified the problem as a lack of infrastructure and organized will to allow brilliance to flourish. He said: “This room is proof of it. The Nigerian Bar counts among its numbers some of the finest legal minds in the world, many of whom have built extraordinary careers abroad, in London, in Washington, in the Gulf. “That is nothing to be ashamed of, but it is something we must be strategic about. For too long we have called this only ‘brain drain,’ as though it is purely a loss. “I ask you to think instead about brain circulation, pulling that expertise back into nation-building without demanding anyone abandon what they have earned and learned abroad. “Our African diaspora already sends home well over one hundred billion dollars a year in remittances alone, more than the foreign aid and investment Africa receives combined. “Imagine that same energy formally invited into legal reform and judicial modernization, as a deliberate national strategy. “Because the fight against poor governance and economic deprivation is not one we can afford to enter with half our talent unaccounted for. “A Nigerian-trained lawyer on an arbitration panel in Paris, or advising a global institution in New York, is not lost talent; it is talent operating at the highest global standard, available to be called home if we organize the bridge for it to cross. “This, too, is what going Beyond Limits must mean for us: refusing to accept that our infrastructural and governance challenges are any kind of ceiling on what is possible. I did not accept the limits the slum seemed to set for me. “I say this to you not as a theory but as something I have lived. In November 2023, when the early, provisional results of our run-off election made clear which way our country had voted, I did not wait for the count to be completed or for the final results to be formally announced before I picked up the telephone to congratulate my successor. “There were those around me who suggested patience, who argued that a sitting president owes it to himself to contest every figure until the very last vote is certified. “I chose otherwise. I chose to concede while the counting was still underway, because I have always believed, and still believe, that the will of the people must stand above the ambition of any one man in a democratic setting. “Once elections do not follow democratic precepts, it is very dangerous for the peace and security of a country. “When your leadership invited me to speak on the theme Beyond Limits, it resonated with the very core of my life’s journey. “In the law, brilliance without discipline leads to compromised justice. Discipline is the quiet commitment to doing what is right, what is necessary, and what is ethical, even when no one is watching. “As legal minds, your hard work secures the liberties of the common man and fortifies the rule of law. “For the legal profession in Nigeria and across Africa, perseverance means standing firm for justice even when the political or social winds blow fiercely against you. “My distinguished friends, Nigeria holds a key to the promise of our whole continent. When the Nigerian Bar Association decides to go beyond limits, the legal architecture of Africa itself grows stronger. “Let us commit today to breaking the chains of mediocrity: applying discipline to our craft, hard work to our duty, respect to our peers, perseverance to our trials, and faith to our foundational values. “Let us all stand for true justice, for the rule of law that builds greater unity, that makes a nation more attractive to investment, and that creates a stable environment in place of internal conflict. “True justice is blind. It does not know politics. It does not see family or friendship. It knows only the truth, and it interprets the law the same way whether or not anyone is watching. “Let us all interpret the law fairly, and apply it more effectively. Let justice prevail, and be done to all men and women, rather than spending our energy on division. “The true measure of a lawyer is not how many cases you have won, how many titles you hold, or how much you earn. It is this: when the country needs courage, do you have the courage to stand? “The law must never be an instrument of chaos. It must never become a weapon of war. “It must remain what it was always meant to be: an instrument of remedy, of peace, of unity, and of accountability; an instrument for humanity, for transparency, and for truth. “As a lawyer, you must be able to protect the law whether the voice before you is rich, poor, or powerful. “As the law provides, you must be able to stand in defense of those who cannot defend themselves. You must ensure that due process is honored. “Let us respect the law, and let us interpret it faithfully. I say to you, as with Lady Justice herself: carry the scales of substance and of justice, and let nothing tip them but the truth. “My brothers and sisters, Nigerians depend on you. “West Africa depends on you. Africa depends on you. The world depends on you. Democracy depends on you. And free elections depend on you. “So I say to all of you here today: Africa must continue in peaceful coexistence, and we must all stand up for the rule of law. Stand up for fairness. Stand up for impartiality. Stand up for gender equality. Stand up for equality. Stand up for humanity. “Stand up for peace and for democracy. Stand up against discrimination. Stand up for accountability. Stand up for free and fair elections,” he added. Some lawyers had opposed the choice of Weah as the conference’s guest speaker, citing his alleged disregard for the rule of law during his tenure. Their misgivings, however, were likely drowned out by the thunderous applause that greeted his presentation at the conference. The post What the NBA must do to help Nigeria, Africa grow — Ex-Liberian President Weah appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Éducation: les dix meilleurs pays en lecture, sciences et mathématiques
items.description: Voici les classements des dix pays ou territoires arrivant en tête dans l'enquête Pisa 2025 de l'OCDE, publiés mardi, en matière de compétences en mathématiques, compréhension de l'écrit et culture scientifique pour les élèves de 15 ans scolarisés. – Sciences Inclut des connaissances en physique, sciences et vie de la Terre et de l'univers, ainsi que des notions de démarches et d'explications scientifiques. 1/Pékin-Shanghai-les provinces chinoises de Jiangsu et de Zhejiang avec un score de 597, 2/Singapour (560), 3/Macao (541), 4/Taiwan (540), 5/Japon (538), 6/Estonie (527), 7/Corée du Sud (526), ​​8/Royaume-Uni (511), 9/Canada (510), 10/Nouvelle-Zélande (509) et Australie (509) Moyenne de l'OCDE : 482 – Mathématiques Il s'agit de « formuler, employer et interpréter les mathématiques dans différents contextes ». 1/Pékin-Shanghai-les provinces de Jiangsu et de Zhejiang en Chine avec un score de 612, 2/ Singapour (563), 3/ Macao (549), 4/Taiwan (546), 5/Japon (525), 6/Corée du Sud et Hong Kong (522), 8/Estonie (508), 9/Suisse (499), 10/Royaume-Uni (488) Moyenne de l'OCDE : 463 – Compréhension de l'écrit Pour réussir, les jeunes doivent montrer qu'ils sont capables de « comprendre et utiliser des textes écrits, mais aussi réfléchir à leur proposition et s'y engager ». 1/Singapour avec un score de 535, 2/Pékin-Shanghai-les provinces de Jiangsu et de Zhejiang en Chine (527), 3/ Taiwan (508), 4/Japon (503), 5/Corée du Sud et Macao (501), 7/Irlande (500), 8/Estonie (499), 9/Nouvelle-Zélande (497), 10/Royaume-Uni (494) Moyenne de l'OCDE : 461 Une différence de quelques points est jugée non significative en raison des marges d'erreur propres à toute enquête réalisée à partir d'échantillons de populations. Pour le Canada et la Nouvelle-Zélande, l'OCDE appelle à la prudence, parce qu'une ou plusieurs normes d'échantillonnage n'ont pas été respectées. The post Éducation: les dix meilleurs pays en lecture, sciences et mathématiques appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Motorcycle number plates: The growing practice of concealment
items.description: The growing practice among some motorcyclists of bending, covering, or otherwise concealing registration number plates is raising concerns about road safety, accountability, and law enforcement in Ghana. ‎On busy roads in Accra and other urban areas, some motorcycles are seen with registration plates tilted upwards, partially covered with pieces of material or positioned in ways that make the numbers difficult to read. The practice can make it harder for law enforcement officers and other road users to identify motorcycles involved in traffic offences, crashes or suspected criminal activity. For law enforcement authorities, a motorcycle’s registration number provides an important link between the vehicle and its registered owner and can assist investigations and efforts to establish accountability. ‎The implications are heightened as Ghana shifts from traditional roadside checkpoints to technology‑supported traffic enforcement, where cameras and electronic devices are increasingly used to detect violations. ‎ ‎While a motorcycle may be fast enough to disappear into traffic, a clearly visible registration number ensures it does not escape the law and can be identified for further action. The Ghana News Agency urges the Police and relevant regulatory bodies to enforce strict compliance with the requirement that motorcycle registration plates be properly displayed, upright, and clearly visible. ‎

items.title: Cameroun: pourquoi Maurice Kamto fait-il si peur?
items.description: Maurice Kamto, le leader du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun (MRC) et son vice-président, Mamadou Mota, ont démissionné de la tête de ce parti de l’opposition. La pression de l’administration étant devenue trop forte contre sa personne, le président du MRC, ci-devant candidat à la présidentielle de 2018 et mis hors-jeu pour celle de 2025, n’avait d’autre option, pour donner une chance de survie à sa formation politique, que de rendre le tablier. A son corps défendant, l’acharnement contre lui étant devenu excessif et se manifestant par tous les moyens, notamment celui que l’administration a déniché, en l'occurrence, la possibilité de la non reconnaissance de la convention du parti qui a reconduit à sa tête, en décembre dernier, Me Maurice Kamto. Et c'est pour ne pas saborder les chances du MRC, principal parti de l'opposition, qui entend se mettre en ordre de bataille pour les prochaines élections de 2027, que le président et le premier vice-président ont quitté leurs postes. Une stratégie qui pourrait bien être payante, si une nouvelle convention est tenue bientôt, comme le prévoit le parti. Toutefois, les démissionnaires demeurent membres du parti, qui, sans doute pour contourner la déstabilisation orchestrée par le pouvoir, projette la tenue d’une autre convention extraordinaire. Quel sort sera réservé à cette autre instance du MRC? Quel stratagème est déjà en gestation dans les laboratoires machiavéliques du pouvoir, pour nuire au MRC? La succession du président Paul Biya étant inexorablement en cours, les dignitaires du régime en place, engagés déjà dans une lutte fratricide, sans concession, concèderont-ils de la place à un parti d’opposition autant craint comme le MRC? Autant d’équations que Maurice Kamto et ses ouailles du parti, devront chercher à résoudre pour espérer marcher, un jour, vers le palais présidentiel d’Etoudi. En tout cas, l’avenir ne s’annonce pas des plus roses pour le MRC, tout comme pour les autres partis d’opposition, le Cameroun de Paul Biya étant une terre plus ou moins hostile à quiconque refusant de marcher dans la direction du vent. Ce n’est pas Issa Tchiroma Bakary, ancien ministre de Paul Biya, qu’il a challengé lors de la présidentielle de 2025, qui dira le contraire. Contraint de prendre les chemins difficiles de l’exil après une élection dont il continue, en vain pour le moment, de revendiquer la victoire, l’homme qui, prônant la rupture a, certes réussi à mobiliser large à travers plusieurs ralliements. Mais, candidat malheureux, il a dû assister, la mort dans l’âme, impuissant, et de loin, à la victoire et l’investiture de l’inusable Paul Biya, 93 ans dont 44 au pouvoir. Tout porte à croire que le Cameroun, en dehors des élections qui s’y tiennent régulièrement et à date, est plutôt une monarchie de fait, plutôt qu’une démocratie. Comme dans bien des pays sur le continent, l’opposition n’y est tolérée que lorsqu’elle ne…s’oppose pas au pouvoir. Et le MRC doit trouver la stratégie pour, non seulement continuer à exister, mais à chercher à conquérir le pouvoir d’Etat, conformément à ses objectifs de parti d’opposition! Par Wakat Séra L’article Cameroun: pourquoi Maurice Kamto fait-il si peur? est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Two accused of land guard activities weep in court
items.description: Two men accused of engaging in land guard activities and unlawfully demolishing an uncomplete building and a fence wall in East Legon, Accra, wept uncontrollably after an Accra Circuit Court remanded them. Gabriel Abotsi Ahor, 29, a carpenter, and Benjamin Essel, 32, a concrete mixer, knelt in court and pleaded with the complainant for forgiveness amid tears. Their emotional display also moved some of their relatives to tears as the Police escorted them from the court premises. Their lawyer later intervened to calm them down. Ahor and Essel have been charged with conspiracy to commit a crime, namely the prohibition of land guards’ activities; engaging in land guard activities; conspiracy to commit a crime, namely causing unlawful damage; and causing unlawful damage. The court, however, declined a bail application filed by their counsel and remanded them to reappear on September 23, 2026. Three alleged accomplices, identified as Watara, Usha and Shamsudeen Hussein, are said to be at large, with the Police pursuing them. Defence counsel pleaded with the court to grant the accused persons bail, saying they had fixed places of abode and persons of good repute who were prepared to stand as sureties for them. Counsel also assured the court that the accused persons would not interfere with police investigations if granted bail. The prosecution opposed the application, arguing that the accused persons could interfere with investigations. The prosecution said land guard activities had become a growing menace, with perpetrators depriving people, particularly vulnerable property owners, of their lands. It said the Police were taking steps to curb the menace and apprehend the alleged masterminds behind the activities. The prosecution further told the court that Ahor had failed to provide the Police with a verifiable address. It therefore prayed the court to remand the accused persons to enable the Police to complete investigations. The facts presented to the court indicated that the complainant, whose name has been withheld, is a public servant residing at Community 25, Tema. Ahor was a resident of Shiashie, while Essel resided at Ablekuma, all in Accra. The prosecution said in 1997, the complainant’s father purchased two plots of land at Adjiringanor from Seth Laryea Mensah, Head of Family of the Ashong Mitse Odatei Family. After obtaining the relevant land documents, he constructed a 10-bedroom house and other structures on the property. Following his death, the property was transferred to the complainant and her two siblings. In July 2026, the complainant and one of her siblings demolished the existing structures to make way for the construction of a modern house. However, while construction was ongoing, the accused persons, together with Watara, Usha and Shamsudeen Hussein, allegedly harassed and threatened the complainant in an attempt to take over the land. On July 15, 2026, the accused persons, armed with cutlasses and other implements, allegedly invaded the land while the complainant and some workers were there. They allegedly assaulted the complainant and two workers, identified as Atsu Michael and Joshua Ahinful, seized their tools and chased them off the property. The alleged harassment continued, prompting the complainant to petition the Director-General of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) on August 26, 2026. The prosecution said that on September 5, 2026, at about 2000 hours, the Police received information from the complainant that the accused persons and their accomplices were again on the land. A team of police personnel was subsequently deployed to the site. On seeing the police, the accused persons and their accomplices allegedly fled. The police pursued them and apprehended Ahor and Essel, while the others escaped. The prosecution said efforts were underway to apprehend the remaining suspects, while the case was adjourned to September 23, 2026.

items.title: Okay, Sure, a Folding iPhone
items.description: Nothing quickens the pulse of an Apple fan more than these three words: one more thing . Steve Jobs used the catchphrase to introduce the original iPhone in 2007. In his 15 years running the company, Tim Cook deployed it only a handful of times, including before his 2014 announcement of the Apple Watch. Today, nine days into his tenure as Apple’s CEO, John Ternus said the magic words. Apple’s next big invention, the company revealed at a launch event in Cupertino, is a $2,000 iPhone that sports—get ready—a “remarkable hinge.” This is the iPhone Duo, a foldable gadget that opens like a book to reveal a capacious 7.6-inch screen. Billed as the most versatile iPhone, it can be used in folded or unfolded form, and in split-screen or full-screen modes. The screen appears seamless when open, which is a clever engineering feat. Yet an iPhone that blossoms into an iPad Mini seems unlikely to change many lives—especially at the price of a MacBook Pro. And foldable smartphones have been on the market since Samsung popularized the category, in 2019. In the pantheon of “one more things,” the Duo feels like a dud. Apple also announced several other devices today, all pitched in superlative terms by executives to obligatory applause. The most interesting might be new versions of the Apple Watch that will listen for sounds such as sirens and doorbells, take notes on your conversations, or play back the past 15 seconds of what someone just said to you. (Exactly how all of that will work, and how well, is not yet clear.) There are also new AirPods with improved noise cancellation. The new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max—the ones that don’t fold—offer “the longest battery life in iPhone history and the most advanced pro-camera system ever,” the company said. They also come in “a sophisticated and unique new color,” which is burgundy. Apple may have once captured people’s imagination. Now it also captures a lot more of their money. On top of its hardware sales, the tech giant is raking in subscription fees to Apple Music, Apple News, Apple TV, iCloud, and more. Earlier this summer, the company announced price hikes on many of its products and a leasing program in partnership with Klarna for anyone who blinks at the sticker prices. One thing it didn’t announce today was the base iPhone 18, or any of its other less expensive models, which now seem likely to be released after the holiday buying season. Apple has begun to feel like a late-stage tech giant, squeezing residual value from markets it has long since saturated. Ternus, an engineer who led Apple’s hardware division, arrives with the promise of reviving the company’s penchant for creativity. In his first company-wide memo as CEO, he told employees he couldn’t wait to “build the future” with them. The companies that are actually building the future these days, for better and worse, are the ones pushing the boundaries of artificial intelligence. Apple is not among them. If there is to be a real threat to Apple’s core business, it is likely to come from AI. For now, the iPhone is the entry point to users’ digital lives: messages, emails, websites, and apps. As chatbot users deepen their relationships with ChatGPT and Claude, those personal assistants could become the primary gateway to online tasks and information. At least, that’s what many in the AI industry believe. They are racing to build AI-first devices—pendants, glasses, speakers, and so on. Jony Ive, Apple’s former chief design officer, is working with OpenAI on what is rumored to be a smart speaker the size of hockey puck . Apple was irked enough that it sued OpenAI earlier this year, alleging that it had poached employees and pilfered trade secrets; OpenAI has denied wrongdoing. Another candidate to build the first proper AI device is, of course, Apple itself. There were signs today that Ternus grasps the assignment: He led the event with a vision of the iPhone as an “intelligent personal hub” through which Siri and Apple Intelligence become the AI-powered command centers for all of the information stored on and sensed by a customer’s Apple devices—their calendar, contacts, messages, movements, and everything their iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods can see and hear. Those are, he acknowledged, “the most private details of your daily life.” That could work to Apple’s advantage; the company has cultivated a reputation for safeguarding users’ privacy. One problem: Despite years of promises of coming improvements, Siri is still not very good. Earlier this year, Apple agreed to pay $250 million to some iPhone 15 and 16 customers over claims that it had falsely advertised the AI capabilities of those devices. In January, Apple was reduced to contracting with archrival Google to supply the underlying AI for a revamped version of Siri. Even so, it is reportedly having some trouble getting app developers to buy in. (An Apple spokesperson didn’t respond to a request for comment.) Being the boring tech giant right now has some upsides. Unlike the industry’s other titans, Apple is not lighting money on fire in a frantic race to build data centers and superintelligent AI. It also appears to be the tech giant whose products are the least likely to bring about the extinction of the human race anytime soon, for whatever that’s worth. Its emphasis on user privacy, with AI tools that keep people’s data on their device instead of sending them to the cloud, remains an important differentiator for those who care about such things. Maybe Apple can go on a while longer as the unchallenged king of fancy consumer-tech hardware while everyone else fights to the death over AI software and infrastructure. Maybe rebuilding Siri around Google’s AI will buy Apple time to eventually develop its own powerful models, the way it leaned on Intel for chips for years before creating its own. But if Ternus really wants to build the future, he will eventually have to do something that once came naturally to Apple when it was an underdog: take a risk.

items.title: Gauff saves match points to set up Rybakina semi-final
items.description: Coco Gauff saved two match points as she fought from a set down to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina. Blown away in a 26-minute opening set, fourth seed Gauff was twice pegged back from a break up in a scrappy second set before coming through a 16-point tie-break to force a decider. Roared on by a partisan crowd, the American’s resilience proved the difference in what became a mental battle as she closed out a 2-6 7-6 (9-7) 6-2 win – a performance she said was inspired by compatriot Frances Tiafoe’s comeback victory over Alex Michelsen on Tuesday night. Progression to the last four marks back-to-back Grand Slam semi-finals for the two-time major champion and her first in New York since winning the title in 2023. It is the first time the top four seeds have reached the semi-finals of the women’s singles at a major since Wimbledon in 2009, after top seed Sabalenka and third seed Jessica Pegula progressed on Tuesday. “At the end of the first set I was thinking about Frances and how he came back yesterday,” Gauff said. “We all want to do well in front of this crowd. Honestly, I was just trying to leave the court with no regrets.” Earlier, second seed Rybakina recovered from losing a set for the first time this tournament – and going break-point down in the decider – to beat Zheng Qinwen 3-6 6-1 6-4. The 27-year arrived at the US Open trailing Aryna Sabalenka by just 434 points and was guaranteed to secure the number one ranking for the first time in her career by reaching the semi-finals.

items.title: Décès de Mgr Gomez : une importante délégation gouvernementale à la maison mortuaire, les dates des obsèques fixées
items.description: Une importante délégation gouvernementale s'est rendue ce mercredi 9 septembre dans la famille de feu Monseigneur Albert David Guillaume Gomez, ancien Évêque de l’Église anglicane de Guinée, rappelé à Dieu le lundi 7 septembre 2026 à Dakar. Cette délégation est allée transmettre les condoléances de la nation à la famille du défunt, installée au quartier Koloma Château. C'est précisément à 17h54 que la délégation conduite par Rose Pola Pricemou, Conseillère chargée des Nouvelles Technologies et de l’Intelligence Artificielle à la Présidence de la République, est arrivée à la maison mortuaire. Elle était accompagnée d'Elhadj Ibrahima Ousmane Bah, Secrétaire général adjoint des Affaires religieuses, ainsi que des conseillers du Premier ministre Bah Oury. Prenant la parole au nom du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, Rose Pola Pricemou a livré un message de compassion, de solidarité : « monsieur le Président de la République nous a mandatés ainsi que le gouvernement pour venir s'associer à la douleur. Il s'agit d'une perte qui est commune à tout le peuple de Guinée. On ne peut que réitérer toutes nos prières, être solidaires à ces moments afin que l'Éternel Dieu, notre Père apaise la douleur de ses proches, de ceux qui peinent dans cette traversée et qui lui accordent une place de choix auprès de lui. Donc, encore une fois, recevez nos condoléances », a-t-elle déclaré. Poursuivant les interventions au nom du Gouvernement, Elhadj Ibrahima Ousmane Bah, Secrétaire général adjoint des Affaires religieuses, a tenu à souligner l'immense contribution du prélat à la vie de la nation : « nous avons perdu une autre âme qui a contribué à la construction de ce pays. Il s'agit de Son Éminence, Monseigneur Albert David Guillaume Gomez. La Guinée vient de perdre l’un de ses valeureux fils. Donc, une douloureuse occasion face à laquelle le Président de la République, Son Excellence Monsieur Mamadi Doumbouya, ne peut pas rester insensible. Il est sensible à tout ce qui se passe dans ce pays, mais quand il s'agit de la perte d'une âme, surtout qui a construit cette patrie, vous le connaissez plus que nous, il n’y manque pas de sensibilité, il est profondément touché. C'est pourquoi il s'est adressé directement à son Premier Ministre pour venir dès aujourd'hui présenter ses chaleureuses condoléances à la famille éplorée et à toute la nation guinéenne par l'intermédiaire de cette autre famille », a-t-il dit. ​Le haut responsable religieux s'est également chargé d'expliquer l'absence de dernière minute du chef du Gouvernement, retenu par des impératifs d'État : ​ « Le Premier ministre voulait être là à 17h. Il s'était préparé pour venir, mais il y a eu une autre contrainte liée à ses responsabilités qui va un peu prendre du temps. C'est pourquoi il n'est pas avec nous physiquement. » En réponse à ces témoignages de sympathie, Madifing Diané, ami de longue date et camarade de promotion du défunt, est intervenu au nom de la famille éplorée pour exprimer toute leur gratitude envers les autorités de la République : « c'est avec une grande émotion que je prends la parole. Je vous demanderais respectueusement de transmettre nos remerciements et toute notre reconnaissance au Président de la République, au Premier ministre et à l'ensemble du gouvernement pour ce que vous venez de nous apporter comme un message. Un message plein d'amour, un message plein d'amitié, surtout un message plein de compassion. Il n'y a pas d'alternative. […]. On n'ira pas loin, si ce n'est que dire merci et prier Allah qu'il nous couvre de sa grâce et de sa miséricorde. Bénisse ce peuple. Que sa grâce soit sur nous tous et nos condoléances les plus sincères. » Programme des obsèques ​Selon les informations communiquées par la famille de l'illustre disparu, la dépouille mortelle de Monseigneur Albert David Guillaume Gomez est attendue à Conakry le 21 septembre. L'inhumation, quant à elle, est programmée pour le 25 du même mois.
